summary.text: Tara Shephard is a Democratic state representative from Arkansas House District 79 who has served since January 2023 and is the Democratic candidate for Arkansas State Senate District 15 in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She advanced from the March 2026 Democratic primary runoff, and her career includes founding and leading Delta Community Based Services.

paragraphs.text: Tara Shephard earned a B.A. in criminal justice from the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff in 1998 and an M.A. in criminal justice and corrections from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock in 2000.
Her career experience includes founding Delta Community Based Services and working as its CEO, as well as work as a drug and alcohol counselor and a teacher.
Shephard was the Zone 6 representative on the Little Rock School District Board of Education from 2013 until January 29, 2015, when the Arkansas State Board of Education dissolved the board.
She won election to Arkansas House District 79 and took office on January 9, 2023, and she won re-election without opposition on the November 5, 2024 general election ballot.
During 2025 and 2026 she was assigned to the House City, County and Local Affairs Committee, the Public Transportation Committee and the Girls State Committee.

Shephard is not seeking re-election to House District 79; in the 2026 Democratic primary for Senate District 15 she finished second and then defeated Charity Smith-Allen in the March 31, 2026 runoff, 58.7 percent to 41.3 percent.
